subject: SIG Response: ephemeral prompt/store TTL, KV-cache behavior, and training opt-out workflow
messages:

Subject: SIG follow-up: prompt/log retention + training opt-out details

Sofia,

Thanks again for the quick intro yesterday. Medisphere's security & privacy team has a few follow-up SIG items we need to close before the evaluation: specifically around prompt/log retention, KV/prefix cache persistence, and whether customer data can ever be used for model re-training. Can you confirm: 1) default retention TTLs for request/response logs and whether those logs are accessible to engineering; 2) how long the inferred KV/prefix cache persists on the serving nodes; and 3) the mechanism and SLA for opting a customer out of any training pipelines (if we request it)?

If you can attach any example audit logs (redacted) and the runtime config snippet that controls TTLs, that would be ideal. We need this for our internal SIG review on Oct 20.

Regards,
Patrick Miller
Director, Compliance
Medisphere Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: compliance@medisphere.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: prompt/log retention + training opt-out details

Patrick —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a short evidence packet (SIG_Response_Pack_20261016.pdf) and will follow up with redacted sample logs and a runtime config snippet from engineering. If you'd like, we can also do a 30-minute walkthrough next week.

1) Request/response logs (prompt/response): by default we retain detailed request/response logs for 30 days in encrypted object storage (SSE-KMS). Access is restricted to the on-call SRE group and security engineers via time-bound IAM roles; export requires an approved compliance ticket. We provide an opt-out flag at the workspace level to disable persistent request/response capture entirely (only ephemeral pointers remain in-flight).

2) KV/prefix cache: KV and prefix caches are held in-memory on serving nodes and persisted to local encrypted ephemeral storage only for quick restarts. Default in-memory TTL is 6 minutes for prefix entries and 12 minutes for cached KV aggregates; across restarts these values are rebuilt from the request traffic pattern (no permanent blob of customer prompts is stored in the cache). We can configure per-workspace TTLs on Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted workspaces can request shorter TTLs via support.

3) Training opt-out: we do not use customer prompts or responses for model training unless an explicit, signed agreement exists. For customers who require formal opt-out, we provide a one-time enrollment process where the customer's workspace_id is added to a training-exclusion list (audited, immutable) — updates take effect within 24 hours, and the exclusion is honored by all canonical training pipelines and sampling daemons. We also provide attestations annually.

Next actions: I'll pull the redacted audit_log_sample.csv and ask engineering to drop a runtime-config-snippet.txt showing the TTL keys. Looping in David and Grace internally to get those artifacts.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SIG_Response_Pack_20261016.pdf (summary + attestation), SIG_Response_SLA_Snippet.txt (summary)

Sofia —

Attached are the artifacts you asked for. Summary below and the runtime snippet (runtime-config-snippet.txt) is attached as a small, human-readable fragment. audit_log_sample.csv is redacted and contains only event-type, timestamp, route, workspace_id, and action. The real logs include IPs and raw prompts which we removed per policy.

Key points:
- Request/response retention: controlled by config key `telemetry.request_retention_days` (default 30). If `telemetry.capture_enabled=false` we skip persistent capture entirely and only keep ephemeral traces for tracing.
- KV/prefix cache TTL: runtime keys `serving.kv.ttl_seconds` and `serving.prefix.ttl_seconds`. Defaults: 360 (6m) and 720 (12m). These values are in-memory only; local ephemeral disk writes are encrypted and deleted on instance termination.
- Training exclusion: repo: infra/training/exclusions; workflow: submit a support ticket which creates a JIRA (INFRA-TX-####), ops approves, engineers add workspace_id to exclusions table (write-once). Pipeline samplers read exclusions every 15 minutes; effect is visible within one propagation window (~15–60 minutes depending on pipeline). We maintain an audit record with ticket/JIRA id.

I attached: runtime-config-snippet.txt (shows keys), audit_log_sample.csv, and a short checksum file for the artifact bundle. Let me know if Medisphere needs a screenshot of the JIRA or we should redact differently.

—David
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: runtime-config-snippet.txt, audit_log_sample.csv, artifact_checksums.txt

Patrick —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is our evidence pack (SIG_Response_Pack_20261016.pdf) plus two supporting artifacts: audit_log_sample.csv (redacted) and runtime-config-snippet.txt. Short summary of the key items you raised: 

• Request/response logs: default retention 30 days (telemetry.request_retention_days). Workspaces may disable persistent capture via `telemetry.capture_enabled=false` — when disabled, no persistent prompt/response blobs are emitted. Access to persisted logs is limited to SRE/security and requires a compliance ticket.

• KV/Prefix cache: in-memory caches with TTLs of 360s (prefix) and 720s (KV aggregates) by default; transient local encrypted writes are used for faster recoveries but are removed on instance termination. Per-workspace TTL tuning available for Dedicated and Private customers; hosted customers can request changes via support.

• Training opt-out: we will honor a signed training-exclusion request. The process: customer request → support ticket → JIRA created (INFRA-TX-####) → ops verifies → workspace_id appended to exclusion table (write-once) → samplers respect exclusion within 15–60 minutes. We keep an immutable audit trail of the ticket and the exclusion entry and provide yearly attestations.

Next steps: 1) If you want, I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with David for a brief run-through of the runtime snippet and logs; 2) If you want the JIRA screenshot as stronger evidence we can provide a redacted export.

Would you like the walkthrough on Oct 19 or Oct 20?

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Security Solutions
Redwood Inference
